title: Annual maximum and annual mean surface temperature at the lunar poles, measured by LRO Diviner
what: Two maps per pole, poleward of 80 degrees, in 240 m cells: the annual maximum and the annual mean of the surface (bolometric) temperature. They summarise many years of measurements; they are not the temperature at the date on screen.
notIncluded: Separate summer and winter maps are not included. No such maps are published; the seasonal measurements exist only as about 190 GB of tables in the NASA PDS (Williams et al. 2019).
projection: Polar stereographic on a sphere of radius 1737.4 km, true scale at the pole, pole at the centre of the grid. South: longitude 0 points to the top row, 90E to the right. North: longitude 0 points to the bottom row, 90E to the right. Mean Earth / Polar Axis frame, east-positive longitude.
values: One 16-bit integer per cell: kelvin, rounded to 1 K. -32768 = no value: the corners of the square beyond 80 degrees, and cells the authors left empty.

annual-max.label: Annual maximum temperature (Diviner)
annual-max.meaning: Highest surface temperature over the year at this place, from LRO Diviner bolometric temperatures binned by local time (96 bins) and season (2 bins) in 240 m cells; the authors fill gaps in each cell's time series and smooth it before taking the maximum. An annual value: separate summer and winter maps are not included.

annual-mean.label: Annual mean temperature (Diviner)
annual-mean.sourceDescription: Mean temperature, averaged over ecliptic and subsolar longitudes [K]
annual-mean.meaning: Mean surface temperature over the lunar day and the year at this place, from LRO Diviner bolometric temperatures binned by local time (96 bins) and season (2 bins) in 240 m cells. An annual value: separate summer and winter maps are not included.

caveats: Annual values only: separate summer and winter maps are not included.
Cells without a value in the published maps are left empty here: 1.8 % of the cells inside 80 degrees south, 0.01 % of the cells inside 80 degrees north.
The maximum is taken after the authors interpolate and Fourier-filter each cell's time series; it is not the highest single measurement.
A 240 m cell averages over small cold spots and warm slopes; Diviner's footprint and the binning limit what is resolved.
South: data from July 2009 to February 2019. North: July 2009 to January 2024.
citation: Schorghofer, N., & Williams, J.-P. (2024). Lunar polar maps derived from Diviner temperatures organized by subsolar and ecliptic longitude (version 3.0) [Data set]. Harvard Dataverse. https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/EGOOCL . Method: Schorghofer, N., & Williams, J.-P. (2020). Mapping of ice storage processes on the Moon with time-dependent temperatures. Planetary Science Journal, 1, 54. https://doi.org/10.3847/PSJ/abb6ff . Underlying measurements: Williams, J.-P., et al. (2019). Seasonal polar temperatures on the Moon. Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets, 124, 2505-2521.

fileFormat: LXG (gzip-compressed lossless int16 grid; see src/terrain/lxg.ts). Rebuild with: node --experimental-strip-types --no-warnings scripts/build-diviner.mjs

source.binning: 96 local-time bins x 2 seasons, 240 m cells

layers.processing: Published 240 m grid, unchanged in position; temperatures rounded to 1 K (largest change 0.50 K). Cells the authors left empty are kept empty (stored as -32768); nothing is interpolated.
